ai.description: *Cnemaspis koynaensis* is a small gecko reaching 35 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a distinct yellow vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Key features include a granular dorsum and smooth venter.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis koynaensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, smooth, or weakly keeled tubercles along its flanks.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis koynaensis* inhabits the moist deciduous and semi-evergreen forests of the northern Western Ghats, typically found on rock boulders at altitudes of 600–1,100 meters.
ai.behavior: The Koyna Dwarf Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging after sunset to actively hunt for small insects along rocky outcrops and tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis koynaensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis koynaensis* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, where it is found at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
